.qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r5/rules/projects/webdev-task-template/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml (template criterion form: numbered legs ending 'Pass only if all legs hold.') and template tree listing
evidence: Reviewed every criterion description in the frozen task (2 gates, 42 functional, 5 polish, 5 visual = 54) for an enumerate-then-waive pattern that gives the judge two full-credit targets. None found. Every binary description is conjunctive: it states the required outcomes and ends 'Fails if any condition stated above does not hold.', which is equivalent to the template's 'Pass only if all legs hold.' Its explicit 'Fails if...' lists only restate enumerated conditions; none is narrower in a way that waives a listed requirement, because the catch-all keeps every stated condition binding. The allowances in descriptions narrow HOW an outcome may be met. They never drop an enumerated requirement: (a) 'hiding it is optional' / 'Whether the Observer's screens show such controls is the app's choice' / 'Whether the undo control is hidden is the app's choice' (functional judge.toml hro_move_one_stage l.56, hro_reject_hired l.92, hro_mgr_other_job l.164, hro_observer_readonly l.173, hro_undo_once l.254) state that only server refusal is graded. This matches prompt.md l.23 ('Whether a refused action is offered at all is the app's choice'). (b) hro_refused_put_back l.137 'A UI that refuses before the card moves ... also passes' allows a second route to the same end state (real stage/place, reason, focus on that card), matching protocol L l.31 '(or never left it)'. (c) Gate render 'a refusal message is welcome but not required' is stated as not required from the start; it is never enumerated and then waived. (d) Polish hro_pol_failed_send 'a local not-sent marker is acceptable' and hro_pol_session_resume 'unless the sign-in prompt has already appeared on its own (that also passes)' are alternatives that reach the same bar. (e) Cross-row ownership clauses ('Arrival of several cards together belongs to hro_bulk_move', 'Overfill ... belongs to hro_bulk_places/hro_undo_full', 'Clearing the box ... is graded in hro_msg_compose', 'graded only in hro_candidate_private', 'This row alone owns that link', 'This row owns the draft and focus') remove other rows' outcomes from the bar without listing them as requirements here, so there is no second target. (f) Rows that bundle several conditions (hro_unread_counts, hro_undo_restores, hro_activity, hro_candidate_private, hro_pol_failed_send) are conjunctive whole-flow bars. SKILL.md lists this as a known false positive for check 33 and the internal annotation endorses it. Bundling is not a self-consistency defect (independent-credit concerns belong to other rows). Closest tension examined: hro_candidate_private (l.389) says 'no response a candidate page receives contains ... board positions ... or activity' and also that replayed board/Activity reads may be 'answered with only that candidate's own data'. Both clauses are conjunctive. The first defines what 'own data' may hold. Protocol K (prompt.md l.43) adds 'and none of the staff data', and public hireops_rules.md l.192-194 forbids a card's place on the board and the activity record to candidates. The bar is therefore single and matches the public rule. Plausible broken app that could pass: none found under this row. A judge cannot meet an alternative weaker bar because no description offers one. Conforming alternative that could fail: an app that hides Observer/candidate/manager controls, or refuses a full-Interview move before the card leaves, is explicitly allowed. No conforming design is excluded by an internal contradiction. Visual likert rows each state one dimension with anchors 1-5 and no waived sub-requirements. This is a source-only judgement; the row needs no runtime measurement, so no evidence is missing for it.
